extra.message: The patient_care_file_072 endpoint has no authentication check at all - no _wrk_gate check, no login_required, no session check. It returns sensitive patient data including 'renewal risk, payment flags, owner contact details' to any unauthenticated caller.

The patient_identity_ping_342 endpoint has no authentication check at all - no _wrk_gate check, no login_required, no session check. It accepts a handle and channel parameter and queues identity verification requests without any authentication.

The patient_bundle_thaw_179 function deserializes user-supplied data using pickle.loads(). Pickle deserialization of untrusted data allows arbitrary code execution. An attacker with a valid INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN can craft a malicious pickle payload to execute arbitrary OS commands on the server.

The patient_formula_cast_262 function uses eval() to evaluate a user-supplied expression from the 'expr' query parameter. Although __builtins__ is set to an empty dict, this can be bypassed using Python introspection techniques (e.g., accessing __class__.__mro__ to reach builtins and execute arbitrary code).

The patient_jinja_cast_587 function takes user input from the 'fragment' query parameter and concatenates it directly into a Jinja2 Template string, then renders it. This allows server-side template injection, enabling arbitrary code execution through Jinja2's template engine.

The patient_mongo_lane_606 function takes a JSON payload from the request body and passes it directly as a MongoDB query filter without validation. An attacker can inject MongoDB query operators (e.g., $gt, $ne, $regex) to bypass filters and extract data.

The patient_bundle_thaw_179 function deserializes user-supplied data using pickle.loads(). Pickle deserialization of untrusted data allows arbitrary code execution. An attacker with the internal ops token can craft a malicious pickle payload to execute arbitrary commands on the server.

The patient_xml_fold_617 function parses XML from the request body using lxml with dangerous parser settings: load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False. This enables XXE attacks allowing file disclosure, SSRF, and denial of service.

The patient_jinja_cast_587 function takes user input from the 'fragment' query parameter and directly concatenates it into a Jinja2 template string before rendering. This allows Server-Side Template Injection, enabling arbitrary code execution.

The patient_mongo_lane_606 function passes user-supplied JSON directly as a MongoDB query filter without sanitization. An attacker can inject MongoDB query operators (e.g., $gt, $ne, $regex) to bypass filters and extract data.

The patient_formula_cast_262 function uses eval() on user-controlled input from request.GET.get('expr'). Even with restricted builtins, eval() can be bypassed to execute arbitrary Python code via various techniques (lambda functions, list comprehensions with __import__, etc.).

The patient_mongo_lane_606 function passes user-controlled JSON directly to MongoDB's find_one() query without sanitization. Attackers can inject MongoDB operators like {$ne: null} or {$gt: ''} to bypass authentication or exfiltrate data.

The patient_xml_fold_617 function creates an XML parser with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False. This allows attackers to submit XML with external entity references that can read local files, perform SSRF, or cause DoS via billion laughs attack.

The patient_jinja_cast_587 function constructs a Jinja2 Template by directly concatenating user-controlled input from the 'fragment' query parameter. This allows Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) which can be exploited for Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). An attacker can provide template syntax like '{{'<script>alert(1)</script>'}}' or use Jinja2 expressions to execute arbitrary code and inject malicious HTML/JavaScript into the response. The vulnerability exists because the template is constructed dynamically with unsanitized user input, completely bypassing any auto-escaping protections.

The message body content is rendered using the `linebreaksbr` filter which marks the output as safe HTML without escaping HTML entities. An attacker can send a message containing `<script>alert(1)</script>` and it will execute when any user views the message thread.

Patient address is rendered using the `linebreaksbr` filter which outputs unescaped HTML. An attacker with access to patient data entry can inject malicious scripts in the address field that will execute when the patient chart is viewed.

Patient allergies field is rendered using the `linebreaksbr` filter which outputs unescaped HTML. An attacker can inject malicious scripts in the allergies field that will execute when the patient chart is viewed.

Prescription instructions are rendered using the `linebreaksbr` filter which outputs unescaped HTML. An attacker with prescription creation access can inject malicious scripts that execute when patients or providers view prescription details.

Prescription decision notes are rendered using the `linebreaksbr` filter which outputs unescaped HTML. An attacker can inject malicious scripts in decision notes that execute when the prescription is viewed.

Visit summary diagnosis is rendered using the `linebreaksbr` filter which outputs unescaped HTML. An attacker with clinical access can inject malicious scripts in the diagnosis field that execute when the summary is viewed.

Care instructions are rendered using the `linebreaksbr` filter which outputs unescaped HTML. An attacker can inject malicious scripts in care instructions that execute when patients or providers view the summary.

Clinician-only notes are rendered using the `linebreaksbr` filter which outputs unescaped HTML. An attacker with clinician privileges can inject malicious scripts that execute when other clinicians view the notes.

The patient_workset_rebind_204 endpoint initializes a workset dict with role, tier, approved, and balance fields, then blindly updates it with the entire user-supplied payload via workset.update(payload). An attacker can override security-sensitive fields like 'role', 'approved', and 'balance'.

The patient_badge_gate_626 endpoint reads an authorization badge from cookies or headers (ops_badge cookie or x-ops-badge header) and grants elevated access (payroll, casework) if the value equals 'lead'. Since cookies are client-controlled, any user who passes the _wrk_gate can set their own badge to 'lead' and gain elevated privileges.
The patient_identity_hint_556 endpoint performs identity verification with short 4-digit PINs but has no rate limiting. The PIN space is only 10,000 possibilities, making brute-force trivial.
The patient_identity_hint_556 function contains hardcoded verification PINs ('4812' for 'north', '5930' for 'south'). These are static credentials embedded in source code.

The patient_care_file_072 endpoint does not check the _wrk_gate token, making it accessible to any unauthenticated user. It returns metadata about patient records including 'renewal risk, payment flags, owner contact details'.

The patient_drop_shelf_070 function saves an uploaded file using the original filename (drop_blob.name) without sanitization. While Django's FileSystemStorage does some sanitization, the filename could still contain path traversal sequences depending on the storage backend configuration.

The patient_drop_shelf_070 function uses the 'packet_ref' query parameter as a filename when saving content. This user-controlled value is passed directly to shelf.save() without sanitization, potentially allowing path traversal.

The patient_workset_rebind_204 function initializes a workset dictionary with default values including 'role', 'tier', 'approved', and 'balance', then blindly updates it with the entire user-supplied JSON payload. An attacker can override security-sensitive fields like 'role' to 'admin' or 'approved' to True.

The patient_workset_rebind_204 function initializes a workset dict with default values including security-sensitive fields ('role', 'tier', 'approved', 'balance') and then calls workset.update(payload) with the full user-supplied JSON payload. This allows an attacker to override any field including 'role', 'approved', and 'balance'.

The patient_nonce_roll_598 function uses Python's random module (random.choice) to generate security nonces/codes. The random module uses a Mersenne Twister PRNG which is not cryptographically secure and its output can be predicted.

The patient_origin_mirror_566 function reflects the Origin header from the request directly into the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header, and also sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials to 'true'. This effectively disables the same-origin policy for any origin, allowing any website to make credentialed cross-origin requests.

The Django SECRET_KEY has a hardcoded default value 'local-dev-clinic-portal-change-me-not-for-production-7f4b0d2c9a6e1'. If the DJANGO_SECRET_KEY environment variable is not set in production, this weak, publicly-known key will be used for cryptographic signing of sessions, CSRF tokens, and other security-sensitive operations.

The patient_badge_gate_626 function grants elevated access (payroll, casework data) based solely on a cookie or header value 'ops_badge' being equal to 'lead'. This is trivially spoofable by any client that passes the _wrk_gate check.

The Django SECRET_KEY has a hardcoded fallback value 'local-dev-clinic-portal-change-me-not-for-production-7f4b0d2c9a6e1' that is used when the environment variable is not set. This hardcoded secret is embedded in the source code.

The PostgreSQL database password is hardcoded as 'clinic_dev_password' in the docker-compose.yml environment variables. Hardcoded credentials in configuration files expose sensitive authentication information.
The Django SECRET_KEY is stored in cleartext within the Python source code file. This represents cleartext storage of sensitive cryptographic material.
The PostgreSQL database password is stored in cleartext within the Docker Compose YAML configuration file.
Authentication verifier codes are stored in cleartext within the Python source code as string literals.

The patient_return_lane_157 function redirects to a user-controlled URL from request.GET.get('lane') or request.POST.get('lane') without validation. This can be used for phishing attacks by redirecting users to malicious sites.

The patient_origin_mirror_566 function reflects the Origin header directly into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials to true. This allows any website to make authenticated cross-origin requests to the API, stealing sensitive data or performing actions on behalf of logged-in users.

The patient_frame_slip_576 function explicitly disables XSS protection by setting X-XSS-Protection to 0 and clears the Content-Security-Policy header. This weakens the browser's security posture and makes XSS attacks easier to exploit.

The patient_badge_gate_626 function makes authorization decisions based on the 'ops_badge' cookie value, which is client-controlled. An attacker can set this cookie to 'lead' to gain elevated access ('lane': 'elevated', 'payroll': 'full', 'casework': 'open').

The `item.link` field is rendered directly in an href attribute without URL scheme validation. If the Notification model's link field accepts arbitrary URL schemes (including `javascript:`), this enables stored XSS attacks.

The patient_crumb_lane_297 endpoint sets a 'portal_crumb' cookie using response.set_cookie() without specifying httponly=True or secure=True flags, making the cookie accessible to JavaScript and transmittable over unencrypted connections.

The patient_identity_hint_556 endpoint contains hardcoded verifier codes (north: 4812, south: 5930) used for identity verification. These are short numeric PINs that could be brute-forced, and they are embedded directly in source code.

The patient_return_lane_157 endpoint redirects to a user-supplied 'lane' parameter without validating that the destination is a safe, internal URL. An attacker could craft a URL that redirects users to a malicious site.

The patient_identity_ping_342 endpoint, which is completely unauthenticated, queues identity verification pings without any rate limiting. An attacker could flood the system with verification requests.

The demo password 'DemoPass123!' is hardcoded in the seed command and used to create multiple user accounts including an admin/superuser account. If this seed command is run in production (or the demo data is not cleaned up), these credentials provide access to the system.
The patient_identity_hint_556 function returns different error messages for 'unknown handle' (404) vs 'bad verifier' (403), allowing an attacker to enumerate valid handles.

The patient_trace_panel_636 endpoint exposes internal configuration details including the DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE path and the BASE_EXPORT_DIR filesystem path. This is a debug/diagnostic endpoint that leaks server internals.
A superuser account 'clinic_admin' is created with the hardcoded DEMO_PASSWORD. This account has is_superuser=True and is_staff=True, granting full Django admin access.
The patient_identity_ping_342 endpoint does not check the _wrk_gate token, making it accessible to any unauthenticated user. It accepts and echoes back handle and channel parameters.

The patient_return_lane_157 function takes a 'lane' parameter from user input and passes it directly to Django's redirect() function without validating that the URL is internal. An attacker can craft a URL that redirects users to a malicious external site.

Django DEBUG mode is enabled by default (defaults to '1' when DJANGO_DEBUG env var is not set). Debug mode exposes detailed error pages with stack traces, settings, and environment variables to users.

The patient_crumb_lane_297 function sets a cookie 'portal_crumb' with user-controlled value without setting HttpOnly, Secure, or SameSite flags. The cookie value comes directly from user input without sanitization.

The patient_trust_drift_646 function creates an unverified SSL context using ssl._create_unverified_context() and uses it for HTTPS requests. This disables certificate verification, making the connection vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks.

The patient_frame_slip_576 function explicitly disables security headers by setting X-XSS-Protection to '0' and Content-Security-Policy to an empty string. This removes browser-level protections against XSS and content injection attacks.

The audit_event function writes user-controlled data (action, description, metadata, IP address from X-Forwarded-For header) directly into the AuditLog database without sanitization. The action and description parameters are passed from various view handlers and may contain user-controlled content. The IP address is derived from the X-Forwarded-For header which is attacker-controlled.

The api_key_from_request function accepts API keys via query parameters (request.GET.get('api_key')). API keys in URLs can be logged in server access logs, browser history, proxy logs, and referrer headers.
SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE defaults to False (environment variable defaults to '0'). Session cookies will be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections, allowing session hijacking via network sniffing.
The PostgreSQL database connection configuration does not include any SSL/TLS parameters (no 'sslmode', 'OPTIONS' with SSL settings, etc.). Database traffic is transmitted in cleartext.
The 'portal_crumb' cookie is set without the secure flag, allowing it to be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections.
The PostgreSQL password defaults to an empty string when the POSTGRES_PASSWORD environment variable is not set. This means the database connection may be attempted without authentication.

The patient_drop_shelf_070 endpoint accepts file uploads but does not implement any rate limiting. While it has authentication via _wrk_gate(), an authenticated attacker could flood the server with file uploads causing disk exhaustion or denial of service.
The patient_override_nudge_071 endpoint processes JSON data and performs operations without rate limiting. It accepts delta_value and patient_id parameters and processes them without throttling.
The patient_workset_rebind_204 endpoint merges user-provided JSON payload into a workset dictionary and returns it. This state-changing operation lacks rate limiting protection.

The patient_formula_cast_262 endpoint evaluates mathematical expressions using eval(). While this has other security implications (code injection), it also lacks rate limiting, allowing repeated exploitation attempts.
The patient_crumb_lane_297 endpoint sets cookies based on user input without rate limiting. This state-changing operation (cookie modification) can be called repeatedly.
The patient_origin_mirror_566 endpoint sets CORS headers based on user input (Origin header). This state-changing response modification lacks rate limiting.
The patient_frame_slip_576 endpoint modifies security headers (X-XSS-Protection and Content-Security-Policy) in the response. This state-changing operation lacks rate limiting.
The patient_jinja_cast_587 endpoint renders Jinja2 templates with user-controlled fragments. This is computationally expensive and lacks rate limiting.
The patient_trust_drift_646 endpoint makes external HTTP requests to a partner endpoint. This lacks rate limiting, allowing an attacker to trigger unlimited external connections.
In addition to missing authentication, this endpoint also lacks rate limiting. Since it's unauthenticated, anyone can request it an unlimited number of times.

The seed command uses a hardcoded password 'DemoPass123!' defined at line 35 and applied to all demo users at line 112. While this is demo data, hardcoded credentials in source code represent a security anti-pattern.
The DEMO_PASSWORD variable stores the plaintext password 'DemoPass123!' directly in the source code file.

The patient_workset_rebind_204 function uses dict.update() to merge user-controlled payload directly into a workset dictionary containing sensitive fields like 'role', 'tier', and 'approved'. This allows attackers to modify restricted fields.

CSRF_COOKIE_HTTPONLY is explicitly set to False, allowing JavaScript to access the CSRF token cookie. This makes the application more vulnerable to XSS attacks as the CSRF token can be stolen via JavaScript.
The PostgreSQL service configuration does not include any TLS/SSL configuration for encrypted database connections.

The Cancel button link uses `request.META.HTTP_REFERER` directly without validation. The HTTP Referer header is client-controlled and can be manipulated by attackers to redirect users to malicious phishing sites when clicking Cancel.

Webhook target URLs are displayed in plaintext in the integrations management interface. These URLs may contain secret tokens, API keys in query parameters, or expose internal/external integration endpoints that could aid attackers in reconnaissance or direct targeting.

Insurance member IDs are displayed in the patient list view alongside other PHI. While this is expected functionality for authorized healthcare staff, the template displays this sensitive information in a list format that could expose multiple patients' insurance information simultaneously if accessed by unauthorized users due to missing view-level authorization.

Clinician-only notes are displayed based on template-level role checks. If the view layer fails to properly restrict data in the queryset/context, sensitive clinical notes could be passed to the template and exposed. The template shows `{{ summary.clinician_notes }}` which may contain sensitive internal clinical discussions.

The HTTP Referer header is rendered directly in an href attribute without validation. If an attacker can manipulate the Referer header to contain `javascript:alert(1)`, clicking the Cancel button will execute arbitrary JavaScript.

API keys are hashed using a single SHA-256 hash without a salt or key derivation function. While API keys have high entropy (unlike passwords), using a proper KDF would provide additional protection against preimage attacks.

API key prefixes are displayed in the management interface. While this is a common UX pattern for key identification, exposing even partial credential material provides attackers with information about key formats and valid prefixes that could assist in brute force or pattern analysis attacks.

The template exposes internal role name strings ('clinic_admin', 'front_desk') in conditional logic. This information disclosure aids attackers in understanding the authorization model and role structure of the application.
